If sentiment is predominantly positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is predominantly negative (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (alternating 0.33/1.00) in last 3 days, apply a 2% downward correction to forecast at 15–20 day horizon to dampen volatility.  
If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.80) over last 10 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (21–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is low (≤0.20) and forecast shows upward trend, apply a 1.0–1.5% downward adjustment in early horizon to align with pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is flat, apply no correction unless true outcome deviates >3% from 7-day moving average — then adjust by ±1.0% based on direction.
